liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (4 reviews): Reviewer hears the Dark Star jam near the twelve-minute mark as the origin of the Beautiful/Hypnotized jam; Second half of the Dark Star jam is great, but reviewer calls it an early form of that progression [3][9][10][14]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (1 review, 2 other sources): Steven Stills joined in on Lovelight, which reviewer says only hints at everything that happened that night; Steven Stills plays guitar and sings on Lovelight [1][2][13]

## Setlist highlights

- **Ending remarks from Bill Graham**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]

## The recordings

- **gd69-10-25.sbd.jagla.81.sbefail.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 5 songs; 62 min; rated 4.55/5 by 47 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says 1969 soundboard recordings sound better than most later ones, and this tape is an example [4]
- **gd1969-10-25.150136.sbd.miller.flac1644**: soundboard; 5 songs; 65 min; rated 3.33/5 by 3 [2]

## Around the show

- Stills and Crosby played an unplugged set during a break, and Hot Tuna came on stage [13]
- Show fell on the night clocks changed for Daylight Savings, so the evening ran long [13]
- Reviewer ranks this the best 1969 Dark Star and suggests the band's 02-15-1973 playing as a follow-up [10]
- Reviewer counts this Dark Star among their top three [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd69-10-25.sbd.jagla.81.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Robert Jagla and David Gans; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Tape is only a partial show, with David Gans's Sonic Solutions mix praised; David Gans edited this copy to cover a reel change right after William Tell [1][6]
- **gd1969-10-25.150136.sbd.miller.flac1644**: transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  June 16, 2020; source: SBD > Reel Master > DAT (44.1k) [2]. Also: The beginning of High Time is cut on this copy [2]
